mainTopic: Mourning practices of תשעה באב (work, the last meal, overturning the bed) and the reasons ט״ו באב is a day of joy
overview: This amud opens by finishing the story of how רבי יהודה בר אילעאי ate his last meal before תשעה באב. He sat in a lowly spot with bread and water, like a mourner whose dead lies before him. The גמרא then quotes a משנה: working on תשעה באב depends on local custom, but תלמידי חכמים never work. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says everyone should act like a תלמיד חכם, so that he truly feels the fast. ברייתות add sharp warnings. Eating on תשעה באב is like eating on יום הכיפורים, work on that day brings no blessing, and whoever mourns for ירושלים will merit to see her joy. Next comes רבי יהודה's view that one must overturn the bed on תשעה באב. After a back-and-forth about who is able and about the other beds in the house, רבא rules that there is no such obligation. Finally the גמרא turns from mourning to joy and asks why ט״ו באב was one of the happiest days for ישראל. It gives several answers: the tribes were allowed to intermarry, שבט בנימין was let back in, the desert deaths ended, and הושע בן אלה removed the guards blocking the roads to ירושלים. What הושע said continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The mourner's last meal before the fast
steps.stepSummary: The end of the description of how a great sage ate the final meal before תשעה באב: in a lowly spot, plain bread and water, like a mourner.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would sit between the oven and the stove and eat. He would drink a jug of water with it, and he looked like a person whose dead relative is lying in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes describing how רבי יהודה בר אילעאי ate his סעודה המפסקת, the last meal before תשעה באב. He sat in the least honorable spot in the house and ate simply, like a mourner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this line, the גמרא said he would bring dry bread with salt. Here we learn where he sat (between the oven and the stove) and what he drank (just water). The comparison to someone whose dead is lying before him shows that this meal was already full of mourning, before the fast had even begun.

keyTerms.meaning: Oven
Stove (a cooking range with two openings)
A jug or pitcher
His dead relative is lying before him (not yet buried), the deepest stage of mourning

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new topic. It is the end of a story that began earlier on the דף about רבי יהודה בר אילעאי's meal before תשעה באב. It describes the meal before the fast, not eating on the fast day itself.

phrases.english: between the oven and the stove, and he would eat,
phrases.notes: The least respectable place in the house.

phrases.english: and he would drink a jug of water with it,
and he looked like one whose dead relative is laid out before him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story earlier about רבי יהודה בר אילעאי's סעודה המפסקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The last meal before תשעה באב should be eaten in a lowly, mournful way, like a mourner whose dead lies before him.

steps.title: Doing work on the Ninth of Av depends on local custom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: whether people may work on תשעה באב depends on the custom of the place, but תלמידי חכמים never work.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: In a place where people usually work on תשעה באב, they may work. In a place where people usually do not work, they do not work. And everywhere, תלמידי חכמים do not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes a משנה from מסכת פסחים about doing work (מלאכה) on תשעה באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no fixed rule forbidding work on תשעה באב. The law follows the local custom (מנהג). But for תלמידי חכמים the answer is the same everywhere: they stop working so they can focus fully on mourning.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה there (in a different מסכת)
A place where they were accustomed (local custom decides)
Work or labor
Torah scholars
Idle, refraining from work

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main source for why work on תשעה באב is a matter of custom and not a strict איסור. It sets up all the statements that follow.

phrases.english: We learned in a mishna there:

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלָאכָה בְּתִשְׁעָה בְּאָב — עוֹשִׂין,
phrases.english: In a place where they were accustomed to do work on the Ninth of Av, they do work;

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ שֶׁלֹּא לַעֲשׂוֹת — אֵין עוֹשִׂין.
phrases.english: in a place where they were accustomed not to work, they do not work.
And in every place, Torah scholars are idle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the meal before the fast to the question of working on the fast day itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Work on תשעה באב follows local custom, but תלמידי חכמים refrain everywhere.

steps.title: Everyone should act like a Torah scholar
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, in the same משנה, says every person should behave like a תלמיד חכם and not work on תשעה באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: A person should always treat himself like a תלמיד חכם.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the view of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. He says the rule for scholars should apply to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the משנה said only scholars must stop working everywhere. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל goes further: any person may, and should, take on the scholar's behavior and stop working. He is not saying that everyone is a scholar. He is saying that everyone should copy the scholar's conduct for this day.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, נשיא of the Jewish people
Always (here: as a general rule)
Should make himself, meaning he should conduct himself as

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם יַעֲשֶׂה כָּל אָדָם עַצְמוֹ כְּתַלְמִיד חָכָם.
phrases.english: A person should always conduct himself as a Torah scholar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the משנה's rule for scholars to every person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every person should behave like a תלמיד חכם and refrain from work on תשעה באב.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports and explains רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא repeats רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view and gives its reason: so that the person will feel the fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: A person should always treat himself like a תלמיד חכם, so that he will feel the fast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the משנה, and adds the reason behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new piece of information is the phrase כדי שיתענה. Not working is not a separate goal. It helps the person truly feel the hardship of the fast, because work and busyness distract him from it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא (a supporting source)
So that he will fast (really feel the affliction of the fast)

phrases.english: This is also taught in a baraita:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם עַצְמוֹ כְּתַלְמִיד חָכָם,
phrases.english: A person should always conduct himself as a Torah scholar,
so that he will feel the fast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 3 and adds the reason for it.
steps.raayaObject: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view that everyone should act like a תלמיד חכם on תשעה באב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבן שמעון בן גמליאל with the added reason כדי שיתענה.

steps.title: Eating on the Ninth of Av is like eating on יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says eating and drinking on תשעה באב is as bad as eating on יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Whoever eats and drinks on תשעה באב, it is as if he ate and drank on יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different ברייתא with a strong statement from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about how serious the fast of תשעה באב is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fast of תשעה באב was set by the נביאים, while the fast of יום הכיפורים is from the תורה. Even so, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that breaking it is like breaking יום הכיפורים. The point is how seriously the day must be taken.

keyTerms.meaning: Another ברייתא teaches
As if (a comparison of seriousness)
The Day of Atonement, a fast from the תורה

steps.confusionAlert: This is a comparison of seriousness, not a statement of identical law. The fast of תשעה באב is still דרבנן (from the נביאים), while יום הכיפורים is from the תורה.

phrases.english: It is taught in another baraita:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Whoever eats and drinks on the Ninth of Av,
it is as though he eats and drinks on Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another ברייתא from the same תנא that stresses how serious the day is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating on תשעה באב is treated as seriously as eating on יום הכיפורים.

steps.title: Work on the Ninth of Av never brings blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says that whoever works on תשעה באב will never see blessing from that work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: Whoever does work on תשעה באב will never see a sign of blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: In the same ברייתא, רבי עקיבא adds a warning about doing work on תשעה באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allowed work in places where that is the custom. רבי עקיבא does not call it forbidden. He warns that such work will not succeed: no blessing will come from it.

keyTerms.meaning: A great תנא
A sign of blessing (success or profit)

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
Whoever does work on the Ninth of Av
never sees a sign of blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and returns to the topic of work from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Work done on תשעה באב does not bring blessing.

steps.title: Those who do not mourn will not see ירושלים's joy
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say that whoever works on תשעה באב and does not mourn for ירושלים will not see her future joy, and they prove it from a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: Whoever does work on תשעה באב and does not mourn for ירושלים will not see her joy. As it says: 'Rejoice with ירושלים and be glad with her, all who love her; rejoice with her greatly, all who mourn for her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give their view in the ברייתא. They tie work on תשעה באב to failing to mourn, and they bring a פסוק as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים focus on the inner attitude: the real problem is not mourning for ירושלים. The פסוק says that those who mourn for her are the ones who will rejoice with her. That means mourning now is the key to sharing in her joy later.

keyTerms.meaning: Mourns
Her joy (the future rebuilding of ירושלים)
As it is stated (introduces a פסוק)
Great rejoicing

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
Whoever does work on the Ninth of Av
and does not mourn for Jerusalem
will not see her joy,
as it is stated: “Rejoice with Jerusalem
and be glad with her, all who love her;
rejoice with her in great joy,
all who mourn for her.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third view in the ברייתא, focused on mourning, and supported by a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who works on תשעה באב without mourning for ירושלים will not see her future joy.

steps.title: The general lesson: mourners will see her joy
steps.stepSummary: From the פסוק, a general rule is drawn: whoever mourns for ירושלים will merit to see her joy, and whoever does not, will not.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: Whoever mourns for ירושלים will merit to see her joy. And whoever does not mourn for ירושלים will not see her joy.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא turns the פסוק into a broad rule that applies to everyone, not only to those who work on תשעה באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 was about one case: a person who works and does not mourn. Here the lesson becomes general, with a positive side and a negative side. Mourning for ירושלים earns a share in her rebuilding, and not mourning loses that share.

keyTerms.meaning: From here they said (a lesson drawn from the source)
Merits

steps.whatToRemember: Whoever mourns for ירושלים will merit to see her joy. This famous line is the core spiritual message of תשעה באב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the best-known sayings about the meaning of mourning for the חורבן. It is often quoted when comforting mourners and on תשעה באב.

phrases.english: From here they said:
Whoever mourns for Jerusalem
merits and sees her joy,
and whoever does not mourn for Jerusalem
does not see her joy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Generalizes the lesson of the פסוק brought in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Mourning for ירושלים is the path to seeing her joy, and failing to mourn takes that away.

steps.title: Meat and wine before the fast is a serious sin
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the theme of required mourning: whoever eats meat and drinks wine at the meal before תשעה באב is described by a harsh פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: Whoever eats meat and drinks wine at the meal before תשעה באב, about him the פסוק says: 'And their sins were upon their bones.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that backs up the idea that one must mourn, now applied to the last meal before the fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating anything on תשעה באב itself is plainly forbidden, so this must mean the סעודה המפסקת right before the fast, as the translation explains. Eating festive foods like meat and wine then shows a lack of mourning. The פסוק from יחזקאל pictures sins clinging to a person's bones, which shows how serious this is. It also connects back to step 1, where the sage ate only bread and water.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat and wine, foods of celebration
About him the פסוק says
Their sins are upon their bones (יחזקאל לב:כז)

steps.confusionAlert: Even though the text says בתשעה באב, it refers to the last meal before the fast, the סעודה המפסקת. Eating on the fast day itself is already forbidden outright.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for the הלכה that one does not eat meat or drink wine at the סעודה המפסקת.

phrases.english: This is also taught in a baraita:
Whoever eats meat and drinks wine
on the Ninth of Av,
phrases.notes: That is, at the meal right before the fast.

phrases.english: about him the verse says:
“And their iniquities were upon their bones.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the idea that failing to mourn is punished, and applies it to the meal before the fast.
steps.raayaObject: The requirement to mourn for ירושלים, including at the meal before the fast.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא applying יחזקאל לב:כז to one who eats meat and drinks wine before תשעה באב.

steps.title: רבי יהודה Requires Overturning the Bed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: רבי יהודה obligates overturning the bed on תשעה באב, and the חכמים disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה obligates a person to overturn the bed, but the Sages did not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה so it can discuss it. This line opens the topic of overturning the bed on תשעה באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mourner (אבל) traditionally overturns the bed and does not sleep on it normally. רבי יהודה says that on תשעה באב everyone must do the same, as mourners for ירושלים. The חכמים do not require this.

keyTerms.meaning: Overturning the bed, a mourning practice
Obligates, requires
They did not agree with him

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda obligates overturning the bed,
phrases.notes: On תשעה באב, like a mourner

phrases.english: but the Sages did not agree with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the theme of mourning in general and turns to a specific mourning practice listed in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה requires overturning the bed on תשעה באב, and the חכמים exempt it.

steps.title: What About Pregnant and Nursing Women?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records the חכמים challenging רבי יהודה: pregnant and nursing women cannot sleep on an overturned bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: The Sages said to רבי יהודה: According to your words, what will become of pregnant women and nursing women?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים attack רבי יהודה's rule with a practical problem: some people physically cannot sleep this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If everyone must overturn the bed, then pregnant and nursing women would have to sleep on the floor or on an overturned bed, which is too hard for them. The challenge suggests that רבי יהודה's rule cannot work as a blanket obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: According to your words or view
Pregnant women
Nursing women

phrases.english: It was taught: They said to Rabbi Yehuda:
According to your words, pregnant and nursing women,
what will become of them?
phrases.notes: A question that works as a challenge

steps.triggerLanguage: לִדְבָרֶיךָ, עוּבָּרוֹת וּמְנִיקוֹת מָה תְּהֵא עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's view from Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's requirement to overturn the bed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A universal obligation would force people who cannot handle it, such as pregnant and nursing women, to suffer.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: Only for Those Who Are Able
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers that his rule only applies to people who are able to do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I, too, only said it about someone who is able.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers the challenge by narrowing his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה never meant to obligate people who cannot manage it. Pregnant and nursing women are exempt, so the challenge does not undo his rule. It only clarifies its limits.

keyTerms.meaning: I too
Regarding one who is able

phrases.english: He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אַף אֲנִי לֹא אָמַרְתִּי אֶלָּא בְּיָכוֹל.
phrases.english: I too only said it regarding one who is able.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף אֲנִי לֹא אָמַרְתִּי אֶלָּא בְּיָכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה obligates everyone, even those who cannot do it.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה obligates only those who are able.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: Each Side Concedes Something
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא supports this: רבי יהודה agrees that someone who is unable is exempt, and the חכמים agree that someone who is able must overturn the bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: רבי יהודה agrees with the Sages about one who is unable, and the Sages agree with רבי יהודה about one who is able.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that confirms רבי יהודה's limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא goes further than confirming the limit. It says the חכמים also agree that someone who is able must overturn the bed. Now the two sides seem to hold the same view, which raises the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way, a formula for supporting evidence
Concedes, agrees
Regarding one who is unable

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is not the final הלכה. Later, in Step 17, רבא rules that the חכמים did not concede at all.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לַחֲכָמִים בְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda concedes to the Sages regarding one who is unable,
and the Sages concede to Rabbi Yehuda regarding one who is able.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 12 with another source.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה exempts those who are unable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A second ברייתא in which each side concedes to the other.

steps.title: So What Is the Difference Between Them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the two sides still disagree about, if both agree on the able and the unable.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question: if the two sides agree on both cases, where is their dispute?
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the ברייתא in Step 13, everyone exempts the unable and everyone obligates the able. The גמרא needs to find a practical point where they still differ.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a question that arises from the mutual concessions in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between רבי יהודה and the חכמים

steps.title: The Difference Is the Other Beds
steps.stepSummary: The difference is whether the other beds in the house must also be overturned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is the other beds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: they disagree about the other beds in the house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים concede only that someone who is able overturns his own bed. רבי יהודה requires overturning all the beds in the house, as a mourner does.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
The other beds

phrases.english: The difference between them is the other beds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about whether the other beds in the house must be overturned.

steps.title: A Mourner Overturns All the Beds
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא about mourning shows that overturning the bed means overturning every bed in the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: When they said to overturn the bed, it is not only his own bed that he overturns; rather, he overturns all the beds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing where the idea of 'other beds' comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For an actual mourner, the rule is to overturn all the beds in the house. רבי יהודה applies that full rule to תשעה באב. The חכמים go only as far as one's own bed.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Overturns
All the beds, every one of them

phrases.english: As it was taught: When they said to overturn the bed,
it is not only his own bed that he overturns,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כׇּל הַמִּטּוֹת כּוּלָּן הוּא כּוֹפֶה.
phrases.english: rather, he overturns all the beds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the answer in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The existence of a requirement to overturn the other beds
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the laws of a mourner

steps.title: רבא Rules: No Bed Overturning at All
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules like the תנא of our משנה: the חכמים did not concede to רבי יהודה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה follows our תנא, and the חכמים did not agree with him at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the final halacha for this discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's wording, 'the חכמים did not agree with him,' is the rule. The חכמים did not agree even about someone who is able. The mutual-concession ברייתא in Step 13 is not followed, so there is no obligation to overturn any bed on תשעה באב.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה, the practical ruling
Our תנא, the author of our משנה
At all

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows the חכמים: on תשעה באב there is no obligation to overturn the bed, not even for someone who is able.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling on the whole bed-overturning dispute.

phrases.english: Rava said: The halacha follows our Tanna,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ חֲכָמִים כׇּל עִיקָּר.
phrases.english: and the Sages did not agree with him at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the bed-overturning discussion with a ruling that rejects the concession described in Step 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is no requirement to overturn beds on תשעה באב.

steps.title: The Two Happiest Days for ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל from the משנה: no days were as happy for ישראל as ט״ו באב and יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: There were no days as happy for ישראל as ט״ו באב and יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, opening a new topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic switches from mourning to joy. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל names two days as the happiest of the year, and the גמרא will now explain why each one deserves that title.

keyTerms.meaning: Happy, festive days
The fifteenth of Av, ט״ו באב
The תנא who made this statement

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
There were no days as happy for Israel
as the fifteenth of Av and as Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section of the משנה, moving from mourning to joy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ט״ו באב and יום הכיפורים were the happiest days for ישראל.

steps.title: Granted, יום הכיפורים Is a Day of Joy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its question: יום הכיפורים is understandable as a happy day, since it brings forgiveness and is the day the second לוחות were given.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, יום הכיפורים is a happy day, because it has pardon and forgiveness, and it is the day on which the last לוחות were given.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It first explains the easy half, יום הכיפורים, so it can then ask what is special about ט״ו באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בשלמא means 'granted, this part makes sense.' יום הכיפורים has two clear reasons for joy: atonement, and the giving of the second לוחות. The question about ט״ו באב will come next.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part is understandable, setting up a question on the other part
Pardon and forgiveness
The second, final tablets

phrases.english: Granted, Yom Kippur —
because it has pardon and forgiveness,
the day on which the last tablets were given.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins analyzing רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's statement from Step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason ט״ו באב is so joyful, since יום הכיפורים is already explained here.

steps.title: What is special about the fifteenth of Av?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its question: we understand יום הכיפורים, but why is ט״ו באב a day of joy?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the fifteenth of Av, what is it? Why was it so joyful?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the question it started in Step 19. It is setting up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 19 the גמרא gave clear reasons why יום הכיפורים is happy: forgiveness and the second לוחות. The word אלא ("but") turns to ט״ו באב, which has no obvious reason for joy. So the גמרא asks what event made it special.

keyTerms.meaning: But / however. Here it introduces the part that is not yet understood.
The fifteenth day of the month of Av (ט״ו באב)
What is it? What is its reason?

phrases.english: But the fifteenth of Av
what is it (that makes it joyful)?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the question begun in Step 19 by contrasting ט״ו באב with יום הכיפורים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What event on ט״ו באב made it one of the happiest days for ישראל?

steps.title: שמואל: the day the tribes were allowed to intermarry
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that ט״ו באב was the day the different שבטים were allowed to marry one another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: It was the day the tribes were permitted to marry into each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer. According to שמואל, ט״ו באב is the day the ban on marrying between tribes ended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the time of בנות צלפחד, women who inherited land had to marry within their own tribe. This kept each tribe's land from moving to another tribe. When that limit ended, ישראל could marry freely again, and the day became a day of joy.

keyTerms.meaning: The tribes of ישראל
That they were permitted
To enter one into the other, meaning to marry between tribes

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
It is the day on which the tribes were permitted
to enter one another (by marriage).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל יוֹם שֶׁהוּתְּרוּ שְׁבָטִים לָבוֹא זֶה בָּזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ט״ו באב was the day the ban on marrying between tribes was lifted.

steps.title: How did they learn the ban was over?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what פסוק they read to decide that the tribal marriage ban had ended.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did they expound?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short follow-up question. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah itself made the rule about marrying within the tribe. So we need a reason from the Torah to say it no longer applies. The גמרא asks which דרשה allowed this.

keyTerms.meaning: What did they expound (from the פסוק)?

phrases.english: What did they expound?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind שמואל's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which reading of the פסוק showed that the tribal marriage ban was temporary?

steps.title: The ban applied only to that generation
steps.stepSummary: The words "זה הדבר" teach that the rule applied only to the generation of בנות צלפחד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, "This is the matter that ה׳ commanded concerning בנות צלפחד..." This teaches that this matter would apply only in this generation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 22. The word "זה" (this) is read to mean "this generation only."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word "זה" limits the rule. It applied only to the generation that first divided ארץ ישראל among the tribes. Later generations were free to marry between tribes.

keyTerms.meaning: The daughters of צלפחד, who inherited their father's land
In effect / applicable
In this generation

phrases.english: "This is the matter that the Lord commanded
concerning the daughters of Tzelofchad, etc." —
this matter shall not be in effect
except in this generation.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה ה׳ לִבְנוֹת צְלׇפְחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22 with a דרשה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word "זה" limits the rule to the generation of בנות צלפחד.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the day בנימין was allowed back
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן gives a second answer: ט״ו באב was the day שבט בנימין was again allowed to marry into the rest of ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said in the name of רב נחמן: It was the day שבט בנימין was permitted to enter the congregation. As it says: "The men of ישראל swore at מצפה, saying: None of us will give his daughter to בנימין as a wife."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different answer to the same question. This one is about the oath the tribes made against שבט בנימין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the terrible event of פילגש בגבעה (ספר שופטים), the tribes swore not to let their daughters marry men from בנימין. That oath almost wiped out the tribe. The day the ban ended became a day of joy.

keyTerms.meaning: The tribe of בנימין
To enter the congregation, meaning to marry within ישראל
Swore an oath
מצפה, the place where the oath was made

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said that Rav Nachman said:
It is the day on which the tribe of Binyamin was permitted
to enter the congregation,
as it says: "And the men of Israel swore in Mitzpah
saying: None of us
shall give his daughter to Binyamin as a wife."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן יוֹם שֶׁהוּתַּר שֵׁבֶט בִּנְיָמִין לָבוֹא בַּקָּהָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, separate answer to the question of Step 20, not a challenge to שמואל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ט״ו באב was the day the oath against marrying into שבט בנימין stopped applying.

steps.title: How did they get out of the oath?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reading allowed them to stop keeping the oath against בנימין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did they expound?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same follow-up question as before, now about the oath. It is setting up רב's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oath is serious and cannot just be ignored. So the גמרא wants to know what reading of the oath's words showed it no longer applied.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath (the subject of this question)

phrases.english: What did they expound?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reading behind רב נחמן's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How did they read the oath so that it no longer applied?

steps.title: "Of us" — not "of our children"
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the oath said "ממנו" (of us), so it bound only the people who swore, not their children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The verse says "of us," and not "of our children."
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question from Step 25. The oath only covered the men who made it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words were "none of us will give his daughter." They did not say "none of our children." So once the next generation grew up, they were free to marry into בנימין.

keyTerms.meaning: Of us (from among us)
Of our children

phrases.english: Rav said: "Of us" (it says),
and not "of our children."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 25 with an exact reading of the oath's wording.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The oath bound only those who swore it, not later generations.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the day the desert deaths ended
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives a third answer: ט״ו באב was the day the dying of the דור המדבר came to an end.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It was the day on which the deaths in the desert ended.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third answer to the question of what happened on ט״ו באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the sin of the מרגלים, the generation that left מצרים was sentenced to die in the מדבר over forty years. ט״ו באב is the day those deaths stopped. The next step explains why that was such a big deal.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who died in the desert (the generation of the מרגלים)
That they ended / were finished

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is the day on which the deaths in the desert ended.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן יוֹם שֶׁכָּלוּ בּוֹ מֵתֵי מִדְבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third, separate answer to Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ט״ו באב was the day the deaths of the דור המדבר ended.

steps.title: ה׳ spoke to משה again only after the deaths ended
steps.stepSummary: A teaching shows that while the desert deaths went on, ה׳ did not speak to משה. When they ended, the דיבור came back, which is why the day was joyful.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: Until the deaths in the desert ended, there was no divine speech with משה. As it says: "And it was, when all the men of war had finished dying... ה׳ spoke to me." Only then was the speech to me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי יוחנן's answer. It shows why the end of the deaths was a reason for great joy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts "ה׳ spoke to me" right after "all the men of war had finished dying." This teaches that the speaking only started again then. So ט״ו באב was not only the end of death but also the return of ה׳'s closeness to משה.

keyTerms.meaning: As the Master said (quoting an earlier teaching)
Divine speech, ה׳ speaking to משה
The men of war, the adult men of the desert generation
Were finished / ended

steps.whatToRemember: So far there are three answers for why ט״ו באב is joyful: (1) the tribes could marry each other (שמואל); (2) שבט בנימין was let back in (רב נחמן); (3) the desert deaths ended and ה׳ spoke to משה again (רבי יוחנן). The next step adds a fourth answer from עולא.
steps.confusionAlert: These three answers are not arguing that the others are wrong. Each is simply another reason the day was joyful. No answer here is rejected.

phrases.english: As the Master said:
Until the deaths in the desert had ended
there was no divine speech with Moshe,
as it says: "And it was, when (they) had finished
all the men of war, dying.
And the Lord spoke to me."
(Only then) was the speech to me.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר מָר עַד שֶׁלֹּא כָּלוּ מֵתֵי מִדְבָּר לֹא הָיָה דִּבּוּר עִם מֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's answer by showing why the end of the deaths was a cause for joy.
steps.raayaObject: That the end of the desert deaths was a cause for joy on ט״ו באב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים ב:טז-יז, where "ה׳ spoke to me" comes right after the men of war finished dying, as explained by a teaching quoted with "דאמר מר."

steps.title: עולא: The Day the Roadblocks to ירושלים Were Removed
steps.stepSummary: עולא gives a fourth reason for the joy of ט״ו באב. It was the day הושע בן אלה cancelled the guards that ירבעם בן נבט had placed on the roads to stop ישראל from going up for the רגל. The line ends by introducing what הושע said.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: It is the day on which הושע בן אלה cancelled the guards that ירבעם בן נבט had placed on the roads so that ישראל would not go up for the festival. And he said:
steps.whatsHappening: עולא offers another answer to why ט״ו באב was joyful: on that day the roadblocks stopping people from going up to ירושלים were removed. The last word, "and he said", is a setup: the גמרא is about to quote what הושע announced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירבעם had split off the northern kingdom and placed guards on the roads so his people could not travel to the בית המקדש in ירושלים. Generations later, הושע בן אלה cancelled those guards. That reopened the way to עליה לרגל, and that freedom is the reason for the joy. This answer is a different event from those of שמואל, רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן. It is not a challenge to them, just one more reason for the same day.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives this answer
Guards or roadblock posts stationed on the roads
The last king of the northern kingdom of ישראל, who removed the guards
The first king of the northern kingdom, who set up the guards
Going up to ירושלים for the three festivals (פסח, שבועות, סוכות)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kings. ירבעם בן נבט PUT the guards on the roads. הושע בן אלה, much later, REMOVED them. The joy is about the removal.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
phrases.notes: A new answer to the question of why ט״ו באב was joyful.

phrases.english: It is the day on which Hoshea son of Ela cancelled

phrases.aramaic: פְּרוֹסְדָיוֹת שֶׁהוֹשִׁיב יָרׇבְעָם בֶּן נְבָט עַל הַדְּרָכִים
phrases.english: the guards that Jeroboam son of Nevat had placed on the roads
phrases.notes: Roadblock posts set up to stop travel south to ירושלים.

phrases.english: so that Israel would not go up for the festival
phrases.notes: This was the purpose of the guards: to block עליה לרגל to the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: And he said:
phrases.notes: Setup word. The next passage will quote what הושע בן אלה declared.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא אָמַר: יוֹם שֶׁבִּיטֵּל הוֹשֵׁעַ בֶּן אֵלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth reason for the joy of ט״ו באב, after the answers of שמואל, רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ט״ו באב was the day הושע בן אלה removed ירבעם's guards, so ישראל could once again go up to ירושלים for the רגלים.
